title: 2 weeks of work - Now, I'm fully committed on the dream RPG I've wanted to make since I was a kid
author: edm-4-life
selftext:
Extended trailer with more asset and animation show case: [https://youtu.be/A5PsdUPdTNU](https://youtu.be/A5PsdUPdTNU)

AI Slop? Probably, but it's my slop and I've been wanting to do this since I was 7 after playing my first game/RPG Final Fantasy 7. Anyways, please let me know what you think. I can take it...and actually prefer it and fix/improve on it.

All assets created within my workflow and pipeline. Nothing bought/borrowed.

Thanks for watching.

comments.author: Lattarde
comments.body: What's the workflow for the assets?

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body:
Thanks for commenting! I'm glad to give a little insight. I start off with reference images from ideas fed to Gemini. Since Gemini hates/can't give multiple images in 1 pass, I say Give me 4 iterations of my idea in 1 photo with 4 panels. So, it gives me 4 samples at a time. When I'm happy I tell it to give me the character in T-Pose in a plain background. (I've attached my robot ref image, there's a back one too but reddit wont let me post 2 at a time).

I then feed the ref image through Claude with the prompt. Claude sends it to Meshy via API. Then takes Meshy's model, sends it to Blender to clean up size/scale, rig and animate, sent it into Unreal to take flight in game.

**Here's my prompt for my robot(Rivet):**  
Let's add a robot to the game using the reference image attached. The parts on the side of each picture is the wings spread out, ready for flight. He is a robot. His face is digital. So, that can change colors, shape, and form things like faces, shapes, arrows...etc (like a LED light board).

Make this NPC. Be very good and strategic which his rig/animation, especially the wings. His take off and landings would be like a winged human. Except, he does not flap the wings. It's more like a jetpack with thrusters. The wings are more for control, turns, and gliding. Be creative and smart about this.

*--- It may not be a 1:1 recreation since Claude already has a very good understanding of what I want/like without more detail. It already knows that it should be using Meshy and not try to draw/model it itself, and then let Blender script the rest.*  
Use this for a better prompt with no previous context: [https://hastebin.com/share/ejodewoguh.vbnet](https://hastebin.com/share/ejodewoguh.vbnet)

Also, in case anyone's wondering:  
**Cost?** Meshy, 36 credits for Rivet.  
Tokens: Claude's estimate is: \~30m tokens  
  
I'm on a 20x Max plan - I haven't maxed out yet. Weekly, I hit about 70-80% before reset. I'm using Opus 5.5 High. And Each pass typically takes 1 to 1.5 hours, I like to feed it al to of instructions per pass/iteration. I'm currently on round 65, as Claude calls it.

For other assets: I describe it and let Claude come up with it. If it needs animations, I tell it, otherwise it makes a inanimate object that usually doesn't fit in. Hope this helps you with your own workflow!

https://preview.redd.it/c6nqx5265ovh1.png?width=1024&format=png&auto=webp&s=3a3fb826994dada5ec3c8014fabcfa1743f1d1a1

comments.author: No-Somewhere-3888
comments.body:
Looks like a pretty good start!

I’ve been experimenting with a similar concept, and I’m struggling a lot with rigging and animating new characters. I’ve noticed your arms and hands still have some unusual motion, but it’s still better than mine.

Has anyone really developed a way to make excellent rigging on generated characters? Meshy seems to do OK with legs/arms, but can’t get fingers right at all.

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body:
Ya, it took a lot to get the weapon gripping even believable. Guides often tell me to use mixamo but I've had mixed luck and haven't really played with an automated workflow for it yet. Might be worth looking into.

My toughest challenge so far was my dragons. At first, they just looked like a stiff 3d model, moving through the sky. Wings, feet, and landing was so stiff. I decided to feed it tons of youtube videos, images, and told it to research other games and their dragons and made it view videos frame by frame and fed it the YouTube transcripts via txt file. Seems like it got a little smarter after that with other animations. I gotta revisit their limbs. Right now, I added archers and they look so bad. Shoulders are all dislocated and pulling arrows through it's chest...etc lol

comments.author: situ139
comments.body:
Always find these interesting cause it's like people start with the graphics first, then try to make the game work after that. 

Just seems so backwards.

Why not make a game loop that is actually fun and exciting, and then build off that. Like get combat down, then add all the extra stuff.

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body: You're probably right. I actually had a general plan lol. For me, it was more like "Wow, this is actually real and I'm playing it. And, it doesn't look like 1984 Pac-Man or 6 rectangles for each limb, head, and torso." So, I just obsess over that and realize I want a robot and a dragon and a glowing sword and repeatedly prompt for visual updates versus a quest line, layout, cast, and whatever. lol

replies.author: situ139

Tbh that's how a lot of good things start, where you're just messing around, etc. But if you wanted to make it a full game, Id rebuild it, using the assets you have, and start with gameplay first. 

Figuring out the mechanics, etc.

Prob look into how real games get developed and mimic their processes.

Former has an F for first.

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body:
I started with something like: "Make me a trailer, about 45 to 60 seconds, showcase the town, combat, dragon flight, townsfolk, and the carnival. Be a creative director. Use Elevenlabs to narrate, use a British male with a deep voice. Reference Fable type humor."

It's pretty stupid without good instruction. My first take, most of the combat was me jumping and getting hit mid air, showcasing literally nothing but our hero failing attacks. Some shots had village NPCs getting killed by a knight swinging thin air, with no sword equipped. It also had a shot of me getting stuck behind a bush for 4 seconds. And a shot of the hero walking but a lamp post blocked his face for the entire camera pan.

So, I had to write a full script, directing most of what I wanted. But, to answer your question, tell Claude to make a trailer. Blender scripts the rest and you end up with a MP4 video file.

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body:
I have a post below about my robot that may help give you a better idea. Basically, I use Claude to direct several tools: Grab a reference image from Gemini, feed the image with a good prompt to Claude and tell it to use: > Meshy API > Blender via MCP > Unreal Engine MCP to build and put into a world you can test/explore (or into your existing game). This is my bible, my workflow.

I also often ask chatgpt or gemini: "Help engineer a solid prompt for Claude. I want to model a 3d game character using Meshy API, Blender MCP, and have Unreal Engine MCP: I want a 3d model that looks like this attached image, it can idle, walk, run, fight with a sword, swim, fall, die, jump, yawn, and roll."

Also worth noting, API and MCP access will produce better results than built-in browser control (having Claude automate it in a browser). And, Claude Opus 5.5 currently does a much better job than ChatGPT Sol. I can't speak for Astra, when I originally used Astra, it ate up my usage way too fast to be worth it.

If you are having ChatGPT or Claude make the models directly, it'll never be as good, with current models. Blender is free - give it a try. You don't even have to do Unreal or Godot (which are also free). You can just have Claude make a quick local web page you can test visuals and animations with.  
  
  
Look into this also: [https://hy3d.tencent.ai/](https://hy3d.tencent.ai/)  
It has free daily text/image to 3d credits and is pretty good for a free service to do some testing with.
